correctness.rationale: The seven-column local predicate exactly expresses independence and exterior support on C_n square K2 for n>=7; the 729-state de Bruijn graph reduces to one 117-state recurrent strongly connected component with 241 arcs. Every arc satisfies an exact integer potential inequality, making cyclic deficit d=2n-3|B| nonnegative. The complete n<=117 trace and Newton-identity calculation verifies, by arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic, det(I-xC(t)) congruent to 1-x^6-2x^2 t-(x+x^4+x^7)t^2+x^5t^4 modulo t^5, exhausting ALL x coefficients because determinant degree<=117. Formal logarithmic differentiation then proves the six-residue exact maximum-size and maximizing-set formulas at arbitrary n, with n=3..6 checked by complete enumeration. Independently reconstructed the transfer automaton and exact determinant coefficients; separate direct graph ESI enumeration n=3..10 matched α and optimal counts. The complete finite matrix certificate, rather than extrapolation from small graphs, supports the all-n proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural and complete classification of a recently introduced graph invariant on a standard cubic product family. Exact six-residue thresholds, unexpectedly sparse six maximal sets at multiples of six, polynomially many optima in other residues, and an all-sizes rational/transfer counting mechanism are reusable concrete combinatorial facts. The new precision is not a mere parameter substitution of a known general upper bound.

limitations: Only the two-layer circular ladders are classified; not general cubic graphs.
Finite determinant certified with all 117 characteristic coefficients rather than empirical traces, while n=3..6 require separate enumeration.
